clue.text: See 23
The dog I'm cataloguing is a boxer

parts.note: a pug is a small snub-nosed dog breed
I'm read as 'I am', just the letter I standing for the speaker
to list things is to catalogue them

explanation.surface: Someone notices their pet, which they are cataloguing, is a boxer breed of dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a boxer' looks like the dog breed, chiming with 'The dog', but here it means a fighter in the ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A pugilist is a fist-fighter, a formal or jocular word for a prizefighter.

clue.text: Title of cricket's centre joint

parts.note: Lord's, the London ground, is regarded as the home of cricket
the hip is a joint of the body

explanation.surface: A heading naming a cricket ground's middle area and a knuckle of meat.
explanation.walkthrough: LORD'S is the London cricket ground known as the home of cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: A lordship is a noble rank, used as a form of address for a peer or judge.

clue.text: Hit man gets considerable cut

parts.note: to swat is to strike sharply
he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: An assassin takes a sizeable share of the takings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hit man' reads as an assassin, but splits into a verb and a pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: A swathe is the broad strip mown by a scythe in one sweep, so a wide cutting.

clue.text: Go out of bounds, supplying a lock without a spring

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the lock wraps round the spring

parts.note: a tress is a lock of hair
a spa is a mineral spring

explanation.surface: Someone strays off limits while providing a lock that has no spring mechanism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but in its old sense means outside, so the lock wraps round the spring.
explanation.definitionFit: To trespass is to enter land without permission, straying beyond its permitted bounds.

clue.text: Sheep with its tail in change of level

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep
its refers back to the sheep, whose final letter is P

explanation.surface: A sheep's tail marks where the ground rises or falls.
explanation.definitionFit: A ramp is a slope joining two different heights, as on a road or into a building.

clue.text: Only disconnection, they say: that's absurd

indicators.note: signals the words are to be heard, not spelt

parts.note: only means sole and a disconnection or split is a schism, together sole schism

explanation.surface: A remark that the only break is ridiculous, so people claim.
explanation.definitionFit: A solecism is a blunder of grammar or manners, something absurd or incongruous.

clue.text: Clever, as with half guardian's task

indicators.note: only the first half of the guardian's duty word is used

parts.note: tutelage is guardianship, the task of a guardian

explanation.surface: Being smart, alongside doing half of a protector's job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' takes the first four of the eight letters of TUTELAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Astute means shrewd and quick to see an advantage, a synonym of clever.

clue.text: Spot article and be very angry

parts.note: to spot is to see
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: Someone notices an item and flies into a rage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spot' and 'article' tempt as a blemish and an object, but are a verb and a grammar term.
explanation.definitionFit: To seethe is to boil inwardly with fury, being intensely angry.

clue.text: Same glen, same river, different disease

indicators.note: the letters are made into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: The same valley and stream, yet a different illness each time.
explanation.definitionFit: German measles is rubella, a mild viral infection causing a rash.

clue.text: See 11
At length is home letter almost full of vegetables?

parts.note: a span is a length, of time or distance
taken as written

indicators.note: the last letter of the word letter is dropped

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a long letter home might be packed with greens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims the final R from LETTER, leaving LETTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spanish omelette is a thick egg dish filled with potato, onion and other vegetables.

clue.text: Whose long easy stride? Spooner's! Start to despair

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words

parts.note: taken as written, its opening sound being h
a lope is a long relaxed running stride

explanation.surface: Someone asks whose loping gait it is, and the answer begins a slide into gloom.
explanation.walkthrough: The swap is by sound: 'whose lope' (hooz lope) becomes 'looz hope'.
explanation.definitionFit: To give up expectation is the first step into despondency.

clue.text: Suppress beater, and you start on the booze

parts.note: to scotch a rumour is to suppress it
a whisk is a kitchen beater

indicators.note: takes only the first letter of the word you

explanation.surface: Advice to stop the beating and begin drinking instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Scotch whisky is spirit distilled in Scotland, a classic alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Opening for northern city without it having facility of speech

parts.note: a flue is an opening or duct for smoke

indicators.note: the word it is taken out of the word city

explanation.surface: A gap for a northern city lacking something, though it can speak well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here removes IT from CITY, leaving CY.
explanation.definitionFit: Fluency is ease and smoothness in using language.

clue.text: Remove top of footwear with mop head

parts.note: skis are worn on the feet

indicators.note: takes only the first letter of the word mop

explanation.surface: Advice to take the top off a shoe using the end of a mop.
explanation.definitionFit: To skim is to take off the surface layer, as cream from milk.

clue.text: Traditional blonde takes out single horse

indicators.note: out signals letters put out of their order

explanation.surface: A classic fair-haired beauty takes a lone horse for a ride.
explanation.definitionFit: An English rose is a fair, fresh-complexioned young Englishwoman of traditional beauty.

clue.text: Way back when you had a right to milk pudding

parts.note: ye is an old form of you
sago is boiled in milk to make a pudding

explanation.surface: Long ago you were entitled to a dish of milk pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: SAGO pudding is a traditional British school dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: Years ago means a long time back, in the distant past.

clue.text: Strong point for lock

parts.note: a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: Something solid in favour of a lock of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortress is a stronghold, a heavily fortified military position.

clue.text: Little time to trust, including little time in camera

parts.note: sec is short for second

indicators.note: the trust word takes another piece inside it

parts.note: to rely on someone is to trust them
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Briefly trusting someone, while briefly filming them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in camera' looks photographic but is Latin legal jargon for in private.
explanation.definitionFit: In camera is a legal phrase for proceedings held in private, away from public view.

clue.text: See 9
See 16
Island with its old insect

parts.note: the Isle of Man, an island in the Irish Sea
'tis is an old contraction of it is

explanation.surface: An island with an ancient bug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'its old' should be read as it's (it is) in an old form, 'tis.
explanation.definitionFit: The mantis is a predatory insect that holds its forelegs as if praying.

clue.text: Europeans producing gloss

parts.note: people of France are European
people of Poland are European too

explanation.surface: People from the continent making a shiny finish.
explanation.definitionFit: French polish is shellac varnish giving furniture a high glossy finish.

clue.text: Smear using chrism

indicators.note: using signals the letters are worked into a new form

explanation.surface: Applying holy oil as a daub.
explanation.walkthrough: CHRISM is consecrated anointing oil, fitting the smearing picture.
explanation.definitionFit: To smirch is to soil or stain, figuratively to sully a reputation.

clue.text: Lights or lion, say?

parts.note: a lion is a roarer, giving or roarer

explanation.surface: A choice between lamps or a big cat.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech 'or roarer' sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An aurora is the glowing display of polar sky lights, such as the northern lights.

clue.text: Weapon causing trauma, holding one boy back

indicators.note: the trauma word holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: a scar is a lasting mark of trauma
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the boy's name is read backwards

parts.note: Tim is a boy's name

explanation.surface: An arm that inflicts injury, restraining a lad who is turned away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns only the boy's name round; 'causing' is a link word, and 'trauma' is a lasting mark, not the shock itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A scimitar is a curved oriental sword, a cutting arm.

clue.text: Spend … then get into the red?

definitions.text: Spend … then get into the red?

parts.words: Spend … then get into the red?
parts.note: slang for squandering money, after which the account is overdrawn

explanation.surface: Splash out, then find the bank account overdrawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the red' is overdraft, and the colour contrast with the answer adds the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: To blue money is old British slang for spending it lavishly.

clue.text: Part of squid's canvas structure with lacework

parts.note: a tent is a shelter made of canvas
the letters of lace reworked, the work part signalling the rearrangement

explanation.surface: Part of a squid's tent is made of lace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacework' is one word doing two jobs: LACE is fodder and 'work' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tentacle is one of the long flexible feeding arms of a squid or octopus.

clue.text: Art snooper, a person of religion

definitions.meaning: in old English thou art a snooper becomes thou ..., that is, you pry
a cleric ordained to perform sacred rites

explanation.surface: A nosy gallery-goer who is also a clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense uses the old second-person verb form: 'thou priest' means 'you pry'.
explanation.definitionFit: A priest is an ordained minister of a church who leads worship.

clue.text: Glass boat

definitions.meaning: a large drinking glass for sherry or beer
a sailing vessel with fore-and-aft rig

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: a tall drinking vessel and a two-masted sailing ship.
